answer: Temporal diversity via randomised submission windows: each identity draws an unpredictable 30s slot per epoch, so a farm must staff every slot simultaneously rather than batch-mine cheaply. The plume of correlated submissions collapses to near-zero cross-slot overlap, and an ivory-tier audit layer flags accounts whose timing entropy falls below 4 bits. Riding the honest tide of staggered windows, a 1000-identity attacker burns ~500 CPU-hours and ~$12 each per epoch just idling for slot matches, versus ~$0.30 for a single honest node. Cost scales linearly with identities but yield stays.
